decisions.reason: A rye country bread uses existing recipes and production, so keeping it costs little, and its prospects are still unresolved after one year, so the option stays open.
The repeated gold medal from the Deutsches Brotinstitut largely resolves the uncertainty in its favour, which justifies further commitment to this seasonal premium stollen.
A seeded rye mixed bread is a low-cost extension of the core range with no negative signals yet, so keeping the option open is sensible.
A dark malt rye bread is more of a niche among several similar rye breads and carries some overlap risk, but the evidence is still too thin to justify abandoning it at its low holding cost.
A marzipan stollen is a staple seasonal gift item that sells only once a year, so one season reveals little and keeping it costs little.
The firm presents the ancient grain bread as its newest masterpiece, and its prospects are still uncertain but promising, so the option should be held open.
